items.title: More countries join Nepal flood rescue efforts

items.title: Bhotekoshi flood survivors face new battle against illness
items.summary: Medicines are running short, health services remain disrupted, and crowded shelters are raising fears of disease outbreaks among displaced families.

items.title: China closes Tatopani border point citing landslides risk
items.summary: With Tatopani closed and Rasuwagadhi destroyed by floods, Nepal’s traders are now left with Korala as the only functioning overland trade route with China ahead of the festive season.

items.summary: Government figures show 4,247 people remain unaccounted for, including 592 foreign nationals, as search and identification efforts continue in the flood-hit districts.

items.title: From hospital to hospital, families search for the ones the flood took
items.summary: Relatives travel hundreds of kilometres across Nepal, moving between morgues, rescue camps and social media in search of any sign of those swept away or trapped by the Bhotekoshi flood.

items.title: NDRRMA chief Dharmaraj Upreti on early warning system, survivor rescue and relief management
items.summary: In an interview with Kantipur, NDRRMA Chief Executive Upreti details the multi-agency response to the disastrous Bhotekoshi flood, highlighting the critical priority of rescuing survivors, deploying transboundary early warning systems, and managing relief and displacement across affected districts.

items.title: A pilgrimage cut short, loved ones swept away
items.summary: Six passengers jumped off a bus carrying 36 pilgrims from Palungtar, Gorkha, to Gosainkunda as the Bhotekoshi flood struck in Nuwakot. Two bodies have been recovered, while 28 remain missing.

items.title: Crisis of communication in Nepal flash flood
items.summary: Rivers do not stop at borders, and neither should warning systems, data sharing or emergency communication.

items.title: The ‘all-weather’ Rasuwa-Kerung route is no more
items.summary: With the main gateway to China destroyed and alternatives vulnerable to floods, landslides and harsh weather, traders face another uncertain festival season.

items.title: Upper Trishuli tunnel crown found, but no response from inside

items.title: Brother searches tunnel for fifth day for missing sibling
items.summary: Ram Budha has been returning daily to the tunnel of the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project in Rasuwa, hoping to hear the voice of his 20-year-old brother Prabin, who remains trapped inside.

items.title: Government releases Rs675 million to 15 local units hit by Bhotekoshi flood
items.summary: The allocation will fund search, rescue and immediate relief in local units across Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha and Tanahun, with the government having already released additional funds to the worst-hit districts.

items.title: Death toll from Bhotekoshi flood reaches 734

items.title: Flood damage to Nepal’s hydropower sector could run into billions
items.summary: Preliminary estimates suggest the Bhotekoshi floods have caused extensive damage to hydropower projects and transmission infrastructure, while insurance coverage and reconstruction costs remain unclear.

items.title: Nepali Army rescues 2,697 people from flood-hit Rasuwa
items.summary: More than 8,300 troops are deployed in affected districts as rescue efforts continue, while heavy rain temporarily halts work to locate the entrance to a hydropower tunnel.

items.title: Nepal working on detailed assessment as Bhotekoshi flood reconstruction could cost up to $5 billion
items.summary: The assessment will determine reconstruction needs as government plans to seek international support for rehabilitation and rebuilding.
